events.summary: President Trump signed Executive Order 14364 on December 6, 2025, directing the Attorney General and Federal Trade Commission Chairman to establish Food Supply Chain Security Task Forces. These task forces will investigate anti-competitive behavior and foreign control in food-related industries (meat processing, seeds, fertilizer, equipment) to determine whether such practices increase food costs or threaten national security. The task forces are authorized to bring enforcement actions, propose regulatory approaches, and initiate criminal proceedings if evidence of collusion emerges. Congressional briefings are required at 180 and 365 days.

events.basis: By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered: The Attorney General and the Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission shall each establish a Food Supply Chain Security Task Force.

events.title: CDC Advisory Committee votes to limit hepatitis B vaccine recommendations for newborns
events.summary: The CDC Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, whose members were hand-picked by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., voted 8-3 on Friday to remove the longstanding recommendation that all U.S. newborns receive hepatitis B vaccination at birth. The new guidance shifts to "shared clinical decision-making" for infants whose mothers test negative for hepatitis B, effectively deferring the decision to parents and healthcare providers. The committee also recommended delaying vaccination from birth to at least two months and introducing blood tests after the first shot—an unstudied approach. Trump welcomed the change and signed a memo to review child immunization recommendations. Medical experts warn the move will increase preventable infections, create access barriers for low-income families, and confuse routine vaccination protocols.
events.why_relevant: Removal of a decades-long vaccine recommendation for all newborns signals a shift in public health policy away from evidence-based medicine, potentially increasing preventable disease and mortality in children while undermining institutional independence of health agencies.
events.basis: The panel of advisers, hand-picked by the US health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, decided to remove the well-established and far-reaching recommendation that all newborns in the US receive a hepatitis B vaccine.

events.title: Kalshi prediction markets lack insider-trading protections equivalent to SEC oversight
events.summary: The CFTC, which regulates Kalshi, does not prohibit the use of inside information in prediction markets, unlike the SEC's strict insider-trading regime for equities. events.title: Trump signs Executive Order 14365 establishing federal AI policy framework and authorizing legal challenges to state AI laws
events.summary: President Trump signed Executive Order 14365 on December 11, 2025, establishing a national policy framework for artificial intelligence designed to minimize regulatory barriers to AI innovation. The order directs the Attorney General to establish an AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws deemed inconsistent with federal policy, authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to evaluate and identify "onerous" state AI laws within 90 days, and empowers federal agencies to condition discretionary grants on states either refraining from enacting conflicting AI laws or agreeing not to enforce them. The order also directs the FCC and FTC to initiate proceedings on federal AI reporting standards and preemption of state laws requiring "deceptive" AI outputs.
events.why_relevant: The order centralizes AI regulation at the federal level, preempts state authority, and uses federal litigation and funding conditions to override state laws—raising separation-of-powers and federalism concerns.
events.basis: Within 30 days of the date of this order, the Attorney General shall establish an AI Litigation Task Force (Task Force) whose sole responsibility shall be to challenge State AI laws inconsistent with the policy set forth in section 2 of this order.

The data shows that ICE arrests more than 1,000 people per day, with county jails functioning as primary enforcement infrastructure. States with 287(g) agreements show higher jail-based arrest rates; states restricting ICE access (Illinois, New York, Oregon) show measurably lower rates, demonstrating that local policy choices directly determine deportation system capacity.
events.why_relevant: The data documents how federal immigration enforcement has become structurally dependent on local cooperation, creating a federalism pressure point where state and local policy choices measurably constrain or expand deportation capacity and due-process protections.
events.basis: Forty-eight percent of ICE arrests now occur through local jail cooperation, meaning the person wasn't picked up by federal agents on the street or at a workplace raid.

events.title: UCLA survey documents ICE enforcement impact on immigrant student safety and school attendance
events.summary: Researchers from UCLA's Institute for Democracy, Education and Access conducted a nationally representative survey of over 600 high school principals documenting the effects of ICE raids and deportations on immigrant students. events.title: White House Press Secretary Leavitt made false claims about inflation rates
events.summary: During a White House press briefing, Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt claimed the Consumer Price Index was 2.5%, contradicting a reporter's statement that the September rate was 3%—the same rate as when Trump took office in January. When confronted on grocery price increases, Leavitt claimed "inflation is down" despite the reporter noting it remained at the January level. events.title: Oregon psilocybin program experiences industry contraction and regulatory challenges
events.summary: Five years after Oregon legalized supervised psilocybin use in 2020, the pioneering program faces significant operational challenges. Licensed service centers have declined from approximately 36 to 24, and licensed facilitators have dropped substantially. High regulatory costs ($10,000 annual licensing fees, surveillance systems, secure storage requirements) combined with lack of insurance coverage have pushed session costs to $3,000, limiting access primarily to white clients earning over $95,000 annually. Multiple facilities have closed, including Portland's largest venue, raising questions about program viability and equity.
events.why_relevant: The program's regulatory structure and cost barriers are creating disparate access to a mental health treatment, raising questions about equitable implementation of a democratically approved public health initiative.
events.basis: The state's total number of licensed service centers has dropped by nearly a third, to 24, since Oregon's psilocybin program launched in 2023. The state's 374 licensed facilitators, people who support clients during sessions, similarly fell.

source_meta.headline: ‘The attrition is setting in’: how Oregon’s magic mushroom experiment lost its way
